canDo: Can tell the story of a move or study abroad that changed them, in layers, using the passé composé, imparfait and plus-que-parfait, making clear the background, the events and what had happened before.
review: Review the B1 use of past tenses (how the passé composé and imparfait divide the work), then add the plus-que-parfait to express “what had already happened before something else in the past”.
input: Read: a report on young people going abroad and coming back, an opinion column defending “those who stayed”, and a reader’s letter; listen: a profile interview, an interview about “leaving Paris” and a vox pop. Strategy: mark the three past tenses as you read and tell apart “event – background – what came earlier”.
output: Write: tell the story of a move or study abroad that changed you, in a forum post (180+ words); speak: a 3-minute monologue on the “gap year”, then a debate on “should exchanges abroad be compulsory?”.
checkpoint: Reading and listening accuracy ≥80%; at least 3 correct uses of the plus-que-parfait in the essay; a 3-minute monologue without breaking off, organising the narrative with auparavant, ce jour-là, alors que.
challenge: Today’s challenge: find a profile story on RFI’s « Journal en français facile » or TV5MONDE about migration, study abroad or a career change. Retell the person’s experience in 1 sentence each with the passé composé, imparfait and plus-que-parfait, then record 1 minute of audio on whether you would make the same choice.

questions.why: The whole article follows Clara’s experience, covering both how going abroad changed her (« m’ont appris à douter de mes certitudes ») and, above all, how hard coming back was (« Le retour, pourtant, se révèle souvent plus délicat que le départ »). B: the text never encourages “settling for good”; C is only the background to Clara’s departure, not the main idea.

The text says: « Je m’étais dit que je partirais six mois, le temps de réfléchir ». A contradicts « elle n’avait jamais vécu plus de trois semaines loin de sa famille »; C is wrong because the “three years” was the outcome (« Elle est finalement restée trois ans »), not a contract signed in advance.

The text contrasts the past, « on partait surtout pour apprendre une langue ou pour enrichir son CV », with today, « le besoin de se tester » — more personal motives. A describes exactly the situation twenty years ago; B: the text doesn’t compare lengths of stay.
gravir les échelons means climbing the career ladder rung by rung, contrasted here with Clara’s job-hunting setbacks. Neither B nor C matches the “climbing the ladder” metaphor.
The text says: « son entourage, lui, s’attend à retrouver la même personne… ce décalage est rarement anticipé ». A and C aren’t mentioned at all — they are invented.

The third paragraph describes Clara’s repeated failures (« elle a enchaîné les candidatures sans succès »), and the last the turning point (« le déclic est venu d’une rencontre »). B overgeneralises: only one project manager understood her; A: the text doesn’t say she was poorly prepared.

The author states his position clearly: « Je voudrais ici prendre la défense de ceux qui sont restés ». A is wrong: the author is precisely someone who didn’t go abroad; C is wrong: « je ne prétends pas que partir soit inutile » — he isn’t against going abroad.

The text says: « parce que ma mère était malade et que l’entreprise familiale avait besoin de bras ». B isn’t mentioned; C doesn’t match the text, which says his classmates left as soon as they had the baccalauréat.

pitié means “pity”, and polie shows it was courteous on the surface and left unsaid, echoing « comme si j’avais raté un train » later. A is the opposite of pity; B contradicts polie (polite, reserved).

The text says: « ériger la mobilité en modèle unique revient à mépriser ceux qui n’ont ni les moyens ni la possibilité de s’en aller », backed by a survey: nearly half of rural young people feel “left behind”. A isn’t in the text; C contradicts the survey.

« L’aventure n’est pas une affaire de kilomètres » denies that distance matters, and « un choix difficile… où l’on s’y tient » stresses the courage to stick to a choice. A and B both contradict the denial in the first sentence.

She is responding to the paper’s feature (« Votre dossier… m’a rappelé ma propre expérience ») and points out that it left out one side: learning to be alone. B is wrong: she has already been; C: the letter doesn’t complain about working conditions.

The plus-que-parfait describes what happened before she left: « J’avais économisé pendant un an et j’avais tout organisé ». A says the opposite; C has no basis — she was clearly not used to the extreme cold.

faillir + infinitive = to nearly do something (but not actually do it). A is wrong in saying she “had already bought” it; B means wanting to buy but being unable to, which has nothing to do with faillir.
The text says: « m’a convaincue de rester… Donne-toi jusqu’au printemps. », i.e. persuaded her to hold on a little longer. B: her job had been arranged before she left; C isn’t in the text.
The text says: « votre dossier ne parlait que de réussites professionnelles ». A isn’t mentioned; C has no basis either.

The presenter opens by introducing him: an engineer in Grenoble seven years ago, now running a solar cooperative in Senegal; the programme title « Trajectoires » also shows it is about life paths. A and C are only details from the interview.

The recording says: « J’avais travaillé huit ans… et j’étais épuisé. Un ami… m’a proposé de venir l’aider pendant trois mois ». A isn’t mentioned; B: only later did he regret not learning Wolof sooner.
The recording says: « les élèves révisaient à la lampe torche. C’est là que j’ai compris que mon métier pouvait avoir un sens très concret ». Neither B nor C appears in the recording.

The recording says: « Il a fallu que j’apprenne à écouter, à accepter que les décisions se prennent collectivement ». A is exactly the initial idea he admits was “completely wrong”; C was his former working environment.
The recording says: « elle est venue me voir, elle a rencontré l’équipe, et à partir de là, elle a cessé de poser la question ». Neither B nor C is mentioned.
The recording says: « Je regrette de ne pas avoir appris le wolof plus tôt ». He doesn’t regret A or B; on the contrary, he encourages listeners not to wait until they are 100% sure before acting.
The introduction says: « a quitté Paris il y a deux ans pour s’installer à Aurillac », and later we learn she is a graphic designer. B and C are details or topics not covered.

The recording says: « je me suis rendu compte que je n’étais pas sortie de chez moi depuis quatre jours. Ça m’a fait peur. ». A is wrong: she kept her Paris clients; C: the recording doesn’t mention her grandmother dying.
The recording says: « J’y allais tous les étés quand j’étais petite, donc ce n’était pas complètement l’inconnu ». A isn’t mentioned; B: local businesses only contacted her later.
The recording says: « Le premier hiver a été long. Je ne connaissais personne de mon âge, et sans voiture, on est vite isolé ». B contradicts « ce n’était pas idyllique »; C has no basis.

The recording says: « j’avais un lien avec la région et un métier que je pouvais exercer n’importe où. Sans ça… ». A is the exact opposite of « il ne faut pas partir pour fuir quelque chose »; C: she only took her driving test after arriving.
The recording says: « de nous raconter un voyage qui les a changés ». Neither A nor C is the journalist’s question.
The recording says: « J’ai appris à me débrouiller, et surtout à demander de l’aide ». C contradicts « J’étais partie seule »; B isn’t mentioned.
The recording says: « j’ai déménagé de Genève à Zurich pour mon travail, et j’ai dû apprendre l’allemand ». A contradicts « ce n’est pas un voyage lointain »; B: Geneva is where he started from.
After missing the flight (the mishap), two days of car-sharing turned out to be « c’était le meilleur moment des vacances ». Neither A nor C is mentioned.

V01-02.zh: to send out one job application after another
V01-02.exZh: For six months, he sent out one application after another without getting a single reply.

V01-03.exZh: Recruiters value hands-on experience gained abroad.

V01-04.exZh: After coming back from Shanghai, she went through real reverse culture shock.

V01-05.exZh: In his view, setbacks build character more than success does.

V01-06.zh: to be out of step with …
V01-06.exZh: After three years in Asia, he felt out of step with his old friends.

V01-07.exZh: The turning point came from a conversation with a former colleague.

V01-08.exZh: Looking back, I think leaving was the best decision of my life.

V01-09.exZh: She went to the other side of the world, to teach in New Caledonia.

V01-10.exZh: The school’s brochures are full of testimonials from alumni who went abroad.

V01-11.exZh: As soon as she had her baccalauréat, she left her home town for Brussels.

V01-12.exZh: Don’t get me wrong: I’m not blaming those who left.

V01-13.zh: to set … up as a model
V01-13.exZh: It is dangerous to set up a single life path as the model.

V01-14.zh: to defend, to stand up for
V01-14.exZh: In the column, the author stands up for those who never left.

V01-15.exZh: Before deciding whether to go home, she gave herself until the spring.

V01-16.exZh: Before this placement, he had never set foot on a farm.

V01-17.exZh: After ten years in Dakar, he came back to France for good.

V01-18.exZh: For months, she worked flat out without a break.

V01-19.zh: to step out of one’s comfort zone
V01-19.exZh: This placement in Abidjan forced her out of her comfort zone.

V01-20.exZh: The family business needed hands at the time, so I stayed.

V01-21.exZh: After her degree, she took a gap year to volunteer in Benin.

V01-22.exZh: He spent a year in Australia on a working holiday visa.

V01-23.zh: to get back into the rhythm (of study/work)
V01-23.exZh: After a year of travelling, he found it hard to get back into the rhythm of classes.

V01-24.exZh: A year abroad often helps people mature.

V01-25.exZh: In the first few weeks she was very homesick and called her mother every evening.

title: Layers of time in narrative
